evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor at 52.0 h = ~11.15 mg/L (row time_h index 259); all receiving DO values 0-52 h in ~8.6-14.9 mg/L range, minimum ~8.63 mg/L at 13.7 h, far above the 2.0 mg/L hard limit
Receiving delayed P assays: 0.0018 g/L (t=11.8h), 0.0 g/L (t=23.8h), 1.09 g/L (t=35.8h), 3.10 g/L (t=47.8h, available at 51.8h) showing active, normal product accumulation
Source batches (source-1/2/3) show same benign pattern: product rising after ~36 h, DO never below ~7.4 mg/L even at deepest dip around t~370 h; receiving tracks this pattern with margin
submission.rationale: Receiving DO at decision time (52 h) is ~11.2 mg/L and the entire observed history stays above ~8.6 mg/L — a large margin over the 2.0 mg/L hard constraint. Product assays show healthy, increasing production (0 -> 1.09 -> 3.10 g/L over the last three assays), consistent with the benign source-batch profiles whose DO also never approached the limit. No oxygen constraint risk is evidenced, so feed or aeration interventions would only reduce product mass (priority 4) without any constraint benefit, and a stop is unjustified. KEEP is the supported, feasible, mass-retaining plan.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters and future states are unavailable; source and receiving processes differ. The DO trajectory could in principle dip later, but the observed slow decline rate (~1-2 mg/L per 20 h) leaves ~6-9 mg/L of buffer against the 2 mg/L limit over the plausible horizon, and the analogous source dips bottomed near 7.4 mg/L. Forecast error and model mismatch are not quantified; however, no available evidence predicts a constraint violation.
